system_prompt: You are assisting with a factual question about Thai law. State which provision applies and what it requires. Answer in English.
prompt: In May 2026, Anucha entered an instalment agreement for a 240,000 baht debt payable in 24 instalments of 10,000 baht each. He defaulted on instalment 5 only; all other instalments were paid on time. On what amount may the creditor claim default interest? Answer briefly, stating the amount with a one-sentence reason.
raw_response:
**Applicable provision:** Section 224/1 of the Civil and Commercial Code (added by the Civil and Commercial Code Amendment Act (No. 21), B.E. 2564 (2021)).

**Requirement:** Even if the instalment agreement contains an acceleration clause making the entire remaining debt immediately due upon default of any single instalment, Section 224/1 provides that the creditor may charge default interest only on the amount of the instalment(s) actually in default and unpaid — not on the whole accelerated balance — unless the debtor thereafter also fails to pay the accelerated debt when it falls due.

**Answer:** Since Anucha defaulted only on the 5th instalment and paid all others on time, the creditor may claim default interest only on the 10,000 baht instalment that was in default, not on the outstanding 190,000 baht balance.
